test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT true for seasonal variation?

options.text: Variation in a time series within one year

solution:
**The Correct Answer is: **Repeated irregularly 

__**Explanation:**__ 

**Seasonal variation:**

__
 
• ​Occurs regularly
 
• Repeats in a fixed pattern every year
 
• Is caused by factors like public holidays and rainfall
 
• Represents variation within one year

 

“Repeated irregularly” describes irregular (random) variation, not seasonal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 1) **Caused by public holidays **

Public holidays create predictable changes in activities, sales, or traffic every year.

Example: Retail sales spike every December due to Christmas.

This is seasonal because it repeats at the same time every year.

 
• 2) **Caused by rainfall **

Rainfall affects crops, tourism, or demand for certain goods (like umbrellas).

Example: Monsoon season increases water-related activities in India.

Seasonal variation is caused by natural cycles like weather, which are predictable and recurring.

 
• 4)** Variation in a time series within one year **

Seasonal variation occurs within a year, not over multiple years.

Example: Monthly temperature changes in a year (summer hotter, winter colder).

This distinguishes it from trend (long-term changes) or cyclical variations (longer than a year).
